dialogue.speaker: فاطمة
dialogue.english: Good morning, Muhammad.

dialogue.speaker: محمد
dialogue.english: Good morning, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: فاطمة
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله، بس أنا نايمة شوية.
dialogue.english: Thank God, but I'm still a bit sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: محمد
dialogue.english: What time is it now?

dialogue.speaker: فاطمة
dialogue.english: It's a little past seven.

dialogue.speaker: محمد
dialogue.arabic: يالله، لازم أروح الشغل، أشتي قهوة بدري.
dialogue.transliteration: yalla, laazim aru7 ash-shughl, ashti 2ahwa bidri.
dialogue.english: Come on, I have to go to work, I want coffee first.

dialogue.speaker: فاطمة
dialogue.english: Okay, drink and go.

dialogue.speaker: محمد
dialogue.english: Thank you, see you in the evening.

dialogue.speaker: فاطمة
dialogue.english: Goodbye, take care.

dialogue.speaker: محمد
dialogue.english: God keep you well.

dialogue.speaker: فاطمة
dialogue.english: And you, my dear.

response.english: Yes, I woke up at six.

pair.english: Do you want coffee first thing?

response.arabic: إِي أَكِيد، ما أَقْدِر بِدُون قَهْوَة
response.english: Yes of course, I can't do without coffee.

lessons.culture: Sanaani mornings start with "صباح الخير" answered by "صباح النور". A small cup of coffee before leaving the house is nearly universal, even on a rushed morning. The greeting and coffee ritual are central to Yemeni hospitality and morning customs.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "صباح الخير". Reply naturally.

too_formal.item: صباح الخير عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته
too_formal.feedback: This greeting is correct but far more elaborate than the everyday morning reply.

exercises.tip: The fixed everyday reply to "صباح الخير" is "صباح النور".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: "إيش الساعة ذلحين؟" Answer that it's seven o'clock.

too_formal.feedback: This is a bookish way to say the time; nobody says it like this in speech.

exercises.tip: "الساعة + number" is the everyday pattern for telling time in Yemeni.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "أَشْتِي _____ بِدْرِي." English meaning: I want coffee first thing.

too_formal.feedback: This wording is more explicit and formal than the simple everyday word.

exercises.tip: "بِدْرِي" means first thing, right after waking up.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "الصُّبْح بِدْرِي _____ كَثِير." English meaning: Early morning is very cold.

too_formal.item: في الصباح الباكر الطقس بارد جداً
too_formal.feedback: This phrasing is correct but reads like a written weather report, not spoken Yemeni.

exercises.tip: "كَثِير" is the Yemeni word for "very", not "وايد" which is Gulf.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Yemeni Arabic: "I woke up early."

too_formal.feedback: This is Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Yemeni speech.

exercises.tip: "قُمْت" is the everyday Yemeni verb for "woke up", and "بِدْرِي" means "early".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I missed the bus."

too_formal.feedback: This is formal written Arabic; the spoken phrase is much simpler.

exercises.tip: "فات" means "missed" and "الباص" is the bus.

exercises.prompt: How do you ask "What time is it now?" in Yemeni?

too_formal.feedback: This is Modern Standard Arabic. In Yemeni we say "إيش" or "ويش" for "what" and "ذلحين" for "now".

exercises.tip: "إيش" and "ويش" are both Yemeni ways to say "what". "ذلحين" is Yemeni for "now", not "هسع" or "الحين".

exercises.prompt: Which word means "very" in Yemeni?

too_formal.feedback: "جداً" is Modern Standard Arabic. Yemeni uses "كثير" to mean "very".

exercises.tip: "كثير" is the Yemeni word for "very". "وايد" is Gulf Arabic, not Yemeni.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the words to make a sentence: "أشتي / قهوة / بدري"

too_formal.feedback: This is more formal. The spoken version is simpler: "أشتي قهوة بدري".

exercises.tip: The word order is: "I want" + "coffee" + "early".

exercises.prompt: Arrange the words to make a question: "ذلحين / الساعة / إيش"

too_formal.feedback: This wording is too formal. The natural spoken form is "إيش الساعة ذلحين".

exercises.tip: The word order is: "what" + "the time" + "now?"

dialogue.speaker: سالم
dialogue.english: Good morning, Ali.

dialogue.speaker: علي
dialogue.english: Good morning, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: سالم
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله، وصلت لللشغل تو التو.
dialogue.english: Thank God, I just arrived at work.

dialogue.speaker: علي
dialogue.english: I have a meeting at ten.

dialogue.speaker: سالم
dialogue.english: And I have a lot of work today.

dialogue.speaker: علي
dialogue.arabic: تمام، أنا جوعان، أشتي أروح للغدا.
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, ana joo3aan, ashti aru7 lil-ghida.
dialogue.english: Okay, I'm hungry, I want to get lunch.

dialogue.speaker: سالم
dialogue.english: Wait, come let's go together.

dialogue.speaker: علي
dialogue.arabic: تمام، بس بسرعة لازم أرجع قبل الاجتماع.
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, bas bsur3a laazim arja3 2abal il-ijtimaa3.
dialogue.english: Okay, but quickly, I have to be back before the meeting.

dialogue.speaker: سالم
dialogue.english: No problem, it's nearby.

dialogue.speaker: علي
dialogue.english: I'll call you in the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: سالم
dialogue.english: Okay, sure.

response.english: Take a break for a while.

pair.english: I have a lot of work now.
I'll call you in the afternoon.

response.english: Okay, I'll be waiting for you.

lessons.culture: In Yemeni workplaces, greetings and small talk about arrival are important. A midday break for lunch with colleagues is common. Yemenis often use the phrase "ذلحين" (now) when talking about current situations or pressing tasks.

exercises.prompt: Your colleague says: "أنا جوعان". Suggest going to lunch together.

too_formal.feedback: This is formal written Arabic. In Yemeni we say "تعال ناكول شي" or "تعال نروح للغدا".

exercises.tip: "تعال" means "come" and "ناكول شي" means "let's eat something".

exercises.prompt: Someone says: "عندي شغل كثير ذلحين". Show understanding.

too_formal.item: أفهم أن لديك الكثير من العمل
too_formal.feedback: This is too formal. Yemenis respond naturally with "يا الله، شغل كثير" or "لازم تخلص بسرعة".

exercises.tip: "يا الله" is a common Yemeni exclamation of acknowledgment or surprise.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "أَنَا جُوْعَان، أَشْتِي _____ شَي." English: I'm hungry, I want to eat something.

too_formal.feedback: This is formal. Yemenis say "أاكول" in speech.

exercises.tip: "أاكول" is the Yemeni way to say "eat" in the present.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "عِنْدِي شُغْل كَثِير _____." English: I have a lot of work now.

too_formal.feedback: This is Modern Standard Arabic. Yemenis say "ذلحين" for "now".

exercises.tip: "ذلحين" is Yemeni for "now". Remember: not "هسع" (Iraqi) and not "الحين" (Gulf).

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I arrived at work."

too_formal.feedback: This is more formal. Yemenis simply say "وصلت للشغل".

exercises.tip: "وصلت" means "I arrived" and "لللشغل" means "to work".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'm a bit tired now."

too_formal.feedback: This is formal written Arabic. Yemenis say "أنا تعبان شوية ذلحين".

exercises.tip: "تعبان" means "tired" and "شوية" means "a bit". Use "ذلحين" for "now".

exercises.prompt: What does "ذلحين" mean in Yemeni?

too_formal.feedback: No, "ذلحين" is Yemeni for "now", not "later". It's an important word to distinguish from "هسع" (Iraqi) and "الحين" (Gulf).

exercises.tip: "ذلحين" is the Yemeni word for "now". Learn to recognize it clearly.

exercises.prompt: Which is the correct way to say "I'm hungry" in Yemeni?

too_formal.feedback: This is formal written Arabic. Yemenis naturally say "أنا جوعان".

exercises.tip: "جوعان" is the everyday Yemeni word for "hungry". It's simple and direct.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "عندي / اجتماع / الساعة / عشرة"

too_formal.feedback: Too formal. The spoken version is "عندي اجتماع الساعة عشرة".

exercises.tip: "عندي" = "I have", "اجتماع" = "meeting", "الساعة عشرة" = "at ten o'clock".

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "وصلت / للشغل / تو"

too_formal.item: لقد وصلت للتو إلى مكان العمل
too_formal.feedback: Too formal. Yemenis simply say "وصلت للشغل تو".

exercises.tip: "تو" or "تو التو" means "just now", commonly used with verbs to show something just happened.

dialogue.speaker: هند
dialogue.english: Good evening, Ahmad.

dialogue.speaker: أحمد
dialogue.english: Good evening, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: هند
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله، بس تعبت كثير اليوم.
dialogue.english: Thank God, but I'm very tired today.

dialogue.speaker: أحمد
dialogue.arabic: تمام، ترتاح شوية. إيش شاناكول العشا؟
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, tartaa7 shwayya. eesh shaanaakool il-3isha?
dialogue.english: That's okay, rest a bit. What are we going to eat for dinner?

dialogue.speaker: هند
dialogue.arabic: أنا ما عندي فكرة، أنت إيش تقول؟
dialogue.transliteration: ana ma 3indi fikra, ant eesh tqool?
dialogue.english: I have no idea, what do you think?

dialogue.speaker: أحمد
dialogue.english: Shall we order from outside?

dialogue.speaker: هند
dialogue.arabic: تمام، بعد ما اجلس شوية وأستحم.
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, ba3d ma aglus shwayya w astahamma.
dialogue.english: Okay, after I sit a bit and shower.

dialogue.speaker: أحمد
dialogue.transliteration: mashi, ana shaaSalli w shaaftah it-tilfiZaaz.
dialogue.english: Okay, I'll pray and turn on the TV.

dialogue.speaker: هند
dialogue.english: We want to watch a series after.

dialogue.speaker: أحمد
dialogue.arabic: تمام، الجو حلو، نطلع نمشي شوية بعدين.
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, il-jaw 7ilw, nItla3 nmashe shwayya ba3dayn.
dialogue.english: Okay, the weather is nice, let's take a walk after.

dialogue.speaker: هند
dialogue.arabic: أشتي استود على أهلي قبل ما نطلع.
dialogue.english: I want to call my family before we go out.

dialogue.speaker: أحمد
dialogue.arabic: تمام، خذي وقتك. أنا شانام بدري اليل.
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, khadi wa2tik. ana shaanaam bidri il-layl.
dialogue.english: Okay, take your time. I'll sleep early tonight.

pair.english: What are we going to eat for dinner?

response.english: Rest a bit and go to bed early.

pair.english: We want to watch a series.

lessons.culture: Yemeni evenings often begin with "مساء الخير" (good evening). After a tiring day, Yemenis relax at home, socialize with family, and may watch TV together. An evening walk to enjoy the cooler temperature is common in Yemeni culture. Calling family in the evening is an important tradition.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "مساء الخير". Reply naturally.

too_formal.item: مساء الخير عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته
too_formal.feedback: This is correct but more elaborate than the everyday evening reply.

exercises.tip: The fixed everyday reply to "مساء الخير" is "مساء النور".

exercises.prompt: Someone tells you: "تعبت كثير اليوم". Show empathy.

too_formal.feedback: Too formal. Yemenis say naturally "ارتاح شوية".

exercises.tip: "ارتاح" means "rest" and "شوية" means "a bit".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "إِيش شَانَاكُول _____." English: What are we going to eat for dinner?

too_formal.feedback: This is formal. Yemenis simply say "العشا" for dinner.

exercises.tip: "العشا" is the evening meal in Yemeni Arabic.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "الْجَو _____ الْمَسِيَة." English: The weather is nice in the evening.

too_formal.feedback: "جميل" is more formal. Yemenis say "حلو" for "nice" in speech.

exercises.tip: "حلو" means "nice" or "sweet" and is commonly used for weather.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I came back home."

too_formal.feedback: This is formal. Yemenis say "رجعت للبيت".

exercises.tip: "رجعت" means "I came back" and "للبيت" means "to the house".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I want to shower."

too_formal.feedback: This is more formal. Yemenis say "أشتي استحم".

exercises.tip: "أشتي" means "I want" and "استحم" means "shower".

exercises.prompt: What does "الجو حلو" mean?

too_formal.feedback: No, "الجو" refers to the weather. "حلو" means "nice" here, not "sweet".

exercises.tip: "الجو" literally means "the atmosphere" but refers to the weather.

exercises.prompt: Which greeting is for the evening in Yemeni?

too_formal.feedback: No, "صباح الخير" is for the morning. "مساء الخير" is the evening greeting.

exercises.tip: "مساء" = "evening", "صباح" = "morning". Learn both greetings.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "رجعت / للبيت"

too_formal.feedback: Too formal for everyday speech.

exercises.tip: Word order: "I came back" + "to the house".

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "نطلع / نمشي / شوية"

too_formal.feedback: Too formal. Yemenis say "نطلع نمشي شوية".

exercises.tip: "نطلع" = "let's go out", "نمشي" = "walk", "شوية" = "a little".

phrases.arabic: الأُسْبُوع الْجَايِ فِي اجْتِمَاع يَوْم الثّلَاثَة
phrases.transliteration: il-usbu3 il-jaay fi ijtimaa3 yom ith-thalaatha

phrases.arabic: عِنْدِي شُغْل كُلّ يَوْم إِلاّ الجُمْعَة وَالسَّبْت
phrases.transliteration: 3indi shughl kull yom illa il-jum3a wis-sabt

dialogue.speaker: خديجة
dialogue.english: When is the meeting next week?

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.english: The meeting is on Tuesday at ten.

dialogue.speaker: خديجة
dialogue.arabic: تمام، أنا يوم الأربعة أشتغل لحد المسية.
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, ana yom il-arba3a ashtighel li7ad il-masya.
dialogue.english: Okay, I work on Wednesday until the evening.

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.transliteration: w ana yom il-khamis ashoof aS7aabi.
dialogue.english: And I see my friends on Thursday.

dialogue.speaker: خديجة
dialogue.arabic: يوم الجمعة ما عندك شغل صح؟
dialogue.english: You don't work on Friday, right?

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.arabic: إي، يوم الجمعة يوم الصلاة والراحة.
dialogue.transliteration: ee, yom il-jum3a yom iS-Salat wir-raa7a.
dialogue.english: Right, Friday is the day of prayer and rest.

dialogue.speaker: خديجة
dialogue.english: And Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.arabic: يوم السبت نروح السوق نشتري حاجات.
dialogue.english: On Saturday we go to the market to buy things.

dialogue.speaker: خديجة
dialogue.arabic: عندك شغل كل يوم إلا الجمعة والسبت؟
dialogue.transliteration: 3andak shughl kull yom illa il-jum3a wis-sabt?
dialogue.english: You work every day except Friday and Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, w ba3dayn il-3uTla taj bisur3a.
dialogue.english: Yes, and besides, the weekend comes quickly.

dialogue.speaker: خديجة
dialogue.english: What do you plan to do on Friday and Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.arabic: نام وراحة وقضاء وقت مع العائلة.
dialogue.transliteration: naam w raa7a w 2ada2 wa2t ma3a il-3ayla.
dialogue.english: Sleep, rest, and spend time with the family.

response.arabic: لا، يَوْم الجُمْعَة يَوْم الصَّلاة وَالرَّاحَة
response.transliteration: la, yom il-jum3a yom iS-Salat wir-raa7a
response.english: No, Friday is the day of prayer and rest.

pair.english: What will you do on Saturday?

response.english: We'll go to the market to buy things.

pair.english: Is there a meeting next week?

response.english: Yes, the weekend comes very quickly.

lessons.culture: In Yemen, as in most Islamic countries, Friday is the holy day, dedicated to prayer and rest. Saturday is often a market day for shopping and socializing. The weekend (Friday and Saturday) is valued as a time for family, prayer, and recovery from the week's work.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "إيش مني الاجتماع؟" Tell them it's on Tuesday at ten.

too_formal.item: الاجتماع مقرر يوم الثلاثاء في الساعة العاشرة
too_formal.feedback: This is formal. Yemenis simply say "يوم الثلاثة الساعة عشرة".

exercises.tip: Use day names directly: "يوم الثلاثة" = "on Tuesday", "الساعة عشرة" = "at ten".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "إيش عتعمل يوم الجمعة؟" Suggest something relaxing.

too_formal.item: سوف أستريح وأقضي الوقت مع أسرتي
too_formal.feedback: Too formal. Yemenis say naturally "نام وراحة" or "أرتاح".

exercises.tip: "نام" = "sleep", "راحة" = "rest" - these are the key Friday activities.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "يَوْم _____ نِرْوح السُّوق." English: We go to the market on Saturday.

too_formal.feedback: "السبت" is the simple Yemeni way to say Saturday.

exercises.tip: Saturday = "السبت" (as-sabt). Remember all the day names.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "يَوْم الجُمْعَة يَوْم _____ وَالرَّاحَة." English: Friday is the day of prayer and rest.

too_formal.feedback: "الصلاة" is the everyday word Yemenis use for prayer.

exercises.tip: "الصلاة" = "prayer", "الراحة" = "rest" - these define Friday in Arab culture.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "The meeting is on Tuesday."

too_formal.feedback: This is formal. Yemenis say "الاجتماع يوم الثلاثة".

exercises.tip: "يوم" = "on" (the day) in Yemeni. Direct and simple.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I have work every day except Friday and Saturday."
exercises.answer: عِنْدِي شُغْل كُلّ يَوْم إِلاّ الجُمْعَة وَالسَّبْت
accepted: عِنْدِي شُغْل كُلّ يَوْم إِلاّ الجُمْعَة وَالسَّبْت
عندي شغل كل يوم إلا الجمعة والسبت
عندي شغل كل يوم غير الجمعة والسبت

too_formal.item: لدي عمل كل يوم ما عدا الجمعة والسبت
too_formal.feedback: This is formal. Yemenis say "عندي شغل كل يوم إلا الجمعة والسبت".

exercises.tip: "إلا" and "غير" both mean "except" - use whichever feels natural to you.

exercises.prompt: Which day is considered the weekend in Yemeni culture?

too_formal.feedback: No, in the Islamic/Yemeni calendar, Friday is the holy day. The weekend is Friday and Saturday.

exercises.tip: Remember: Friday (الجمعة) = prayer day + Saturday (السبت) = market/family day in Yemen.

exercises.prompt: How do you ask "When is the meeting?" in Yemeni?

too_formal.feedback: "متى" is Modern Standard Arabic. Yemenis say "إيش مني" or "إيش الساعة".

exercises.tip: "إيش مني" literally asks "what (is the) time", used to ask "when" in Yemeni.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "يوم / السبت / السوق / نروح"

too_formal.item: في يوم السبت نذهب إلى السوق
too_formal.feedback: Too formal. Yemenis say "يوم السبت نروح السوق".

exercises.tip: Word order: day + verb + destination. Keep it simple.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "الجمعة / يوم / الراحة / والصلاة"

too_formal.feedback: Too formal. Yemenis say "يوم الجمعة يوم الصلاة والراحة".

exercises.tip: The structure is: "day X = day of Y and Z". A simple definition.

reply.english: Yes, I like it very much.

dialogue.speaker: محمد
dialogue.arabic: ما شاء الله! أنا ما أصبرش على القراءة.
dialogue.transliteration: maa shaa2 allaah! ana ma aSbirsh 3ala l-giraa2a.

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.english: And what did you cook?

dialogue.english: Saltah and bint al-sahn.

dialogue.speaker: يوسف

pair.english: What do you do in your free time?

response.english: Yes, I like it very much.

pair.english: Do you have time this evening?

lessons.culture: On Fridays many Sana'ani families visit relatives or drive out to the green valleys around the city, such as وادي ظهر. Free time is often measured by the prayers, so plans are made for "بعد المغرب" or "بعد العصر" rather than by the clock.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "إيش تعمل في وقت الفراغ؟" Say your hobby is reading.

too_formal.feedback: This is formal written Arabic.

exercises.tip: "ق" is said "g" in Sana'a: "giraa2a".

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "معك وقت الليلة؟" Say yes, after the sunset prayer.
exercises.tip: "إيه" is "yes" in Sana'a.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "تحب الخط العربي؟" Say yes, very much.

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; say "إيه، أحبه قوي".

exercises.tip: "قوي" after a word means "very" or "a lot" in Yemeni speech.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "أقرأ كتاب كل _____." (I read a book every week.)
exercises.tip: "كل" + a time word: "كل يوم", "كل أسبوع".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "أطلع _____ مع أصحابي." (I climb mountains with my friends.)
exercises.tip: "طلع" is to go up or climb.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I like cooking."
exercises.tip: "أحب" + a noun with "ال".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "What do you do in your free time?" (to a man)

too_formal.feedback: "ماذا تفعل" is formal; Sana'a says "إيش تعمل".

exercises.tip: "إيش" opens the question; to a woman, "تعملي".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I cooked dinner for my family yesterday."
exercises.tip: "أهلي" is my family, the people at home.

exercises.prompt: Which word means "hobby"?
exercises.tip: "هوايتي" is "my hobby".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I grow flowers in the garden"?
exercises.tip: "زرع" is to plant or grow.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "وقتي / مع / أقضّي / أهلي".
exercises.tip: The verb comes first, then what you spend: "وقتي".

dialogue.speaker: سالم
dialogue.english: There's a match tonight.

dialogue.speaker: علي
dialogue.arabic: أنا ما أحبّش أتفرّج، أحب ألعب.
dialogue.transliteration: ana ma a7ibbish atfarraj, a7ibb al3ab.
dialogue.english: I don't like watching, I like playing.

pair.english: Shall we walk together after the prayer?

lessons.culture: Football is Yemen's favourite sport: boys play it in every street and open lot, and Sana'a's big clubs are أهلي صنعاء and وحدة صنعاء. Archery and horse riding are admired because the Prophet encouraged them, and an evening walk after the sunset prayer is a common way to keep fit.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "تلعب رياضة؟" Say yes, you play football.
exercises.tip: "كورة" is the everyday word for football; "كرة قدم" is the full name.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "أيّ فريق تشجّع؟" Say you support Al-Ahli Sana'a.
exercises.tip: "شجّع" is to cheer for a team.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "نمشي مع بعض بعد الصلاة؟" Say OK the Sana'ani way.

too_formal.feedback: This is formal written Arabic.

exercises.tip: "ناهي" is Sana'a's "OK".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "أركب السيكل _____ في الحديقة." (I ride my bicycle in the park.)
exercises.tip: Yemenis often say "my" with "حقي" after the noun: "السيكل حقي".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "أنا تعبان، _____ ماء." (I'm tired, I need water.)

too_formal.feedback: "أحتاج إلى" is formal; say "أشتي".

exercises.tip: "أشتي" is "I want" or "I need" in Sana'a.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I run every morning."
exercises.tip: "كل صباح" is every morning.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "The match starts at eight."

too_formal.item: تبدأ المباراة في تمام الساعة الثامنة
too_formal.feedback: This is formal, newsreader Arabic.

exercises.tip: Sana'a keeps the "th" sound: "thamaan".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I lift weights at the gym."
exercises.tip: "جيم" is the gym.

exercises.prompt: Which word means "bicycle" in Sana'a?
exercises.tip: "سيكل" comes from the English "cycle".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says exercise is good for health?
exercises.tip: "صحة" is health.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "الجمعة / حصان / يوم / أركب".
exercises.tip: The day goes at the end.

challenge.title: Daily Routine Conversation
challenge.instructions: Create a conversation between two people about their daily routine. Use at least these elements: greet someone in the morning or evening, ask about the time, mention work or activities, and say goodbye. The conversation should be at least 8 exchanges long.
required_elements: A question about the time using "إيش الساعة ذلحين؟"
At least one mention of work or a daily activity

dialogue.speaker: محمد
dialogue.english: Good morning, Hind.

dialogue.speaker: هند
dialogue.english: Good morning, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: محمد
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله تمام، إيش الساعة ذلحين؟
dialogue.english: Thank God, I'm fine. What time is it now?

dialogue.speaker: هند
dialogue.english: It's almost seven.

dialogue.speaker: محمد
dialogue.arabic: يالله، لازم أروح الشغل، أشتي قهوة بدري.
dialogue.transliteration: yalla, laazim aru7 ash-shughl, ashti 2ahwa bidri.
dialogue.english: Come on, I have to go to work. I want coffee first.

dialogue.speaker: هند
dialogue.arabic: اشرب القهوة وطلع، عندي اجتماع يوم الثلاثة.
dialogue.transliteration: ishrab il-2ahwa w iTla3, 3indi ijtimaa3 yom ith-thalaatha.
dialogue.english: Drink coffee and go, I have a meeting on Tuesday.

dialogue.speaker: محمد
dialogue.english: Okay, see you in the evening. Goodbye.

dialogue.speaker: هند
dialogue.english: Goodbye.
